successors.note: The same people: the Alemanni page has them 'conquered by Clovis I at the Battle of Tolbiac' in 496. The cut at 461 is the Cliopatria row's start (462), not an event; eu-06 owns kingdom-of-alamannia and should treat this dossier as its prehistory (merge or link as predecessor).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Alemanni are 'first mentioned by Cassius Dio in the context of the campaign of Roman emperor Caracalla of 213 AD' (Alemanni page) and 'had broken through the Roman limes in 213' (Alamannia page). Neither page draws their land before 260; the Main basin is the only origin named. Franconia is used for it; the area is a guess.

The Agri Decumates are drawn as Baden-Wurttemberg plus Franconia (Franconian Jura); neither page gives an area.

correction.text: the Main River basin: the Alemanni 'expanded from the Main River basin during the 3rd century'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Emperor Probus definitely recaptured the area during his invasion of Germania' (Agri Decumates page, no year); the Germanic Wars page has '277-278: Emperor Probus's successful campaigns against Goths, Alamanni, Longiones, Franks and Burgundians'. The year 277 is bridged. 'Aurelian (270-275) may have had the region briefly reoccupied' (uncertain).

correction.text: the Agri Decumates, 'covering the Black Forest, Swabian Jura, and Franconian Jura areas between the Rhine, Main, and Danube rivers', with the Main basin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Roman military 'seems to have definitively abandoned the region' in 'the 290s or 300s' and 'By about 310 the Alemanni were becoming the dominant population' (Agri Decumates page). The Alamannia page says they 'settled on the left bank of the Rhine River from the 4th century' and 'settled new territory on either side of the Rhine' in the 5th-6th centuries, undated: The left bank is drawn from 406 (alemanni_406); the Alamannia page's 'from the 4th century' left-bank settlement stays undated and is not drawn earlier. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alamannia shapes from 462 lie on the left bank (bbox 3.7-10.2 E, 47.0-50.5 N). [Fix 2026-10-19: this keyframe now ends in 405; the shape from 406 is alemanni_406.]

correction.text: the Agri Decumates with the Main basin (as alemanni_300) plus Alsace: 'In the great mixed invasion of 406, the Alemanni appear to have crossed the Rhine river a final time, conquering and then settling what is today Alsace'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (reviewer eu-04-x fix): the Alemanni page dates the conquest and settlement of Alsace to the invasion of 406: 'In the great mixed invasion of 406, the Alemanni appear to have crossed the Rhine river a final time, conquering and then settling what is today Alsace and a large part of the Swiss Plateau.' The wording 'appear to have' is the page's own hedge; Alsace only is drawn, the Swiss Plateau is not (the gazetteer has no such name and Switzerland would take in the Alps).

region.text: the Main River basin: the Alemanni 'expanded from the Main River basin during the 3rd century'

ledger.note: 213: the Alemanni appear on the Roman frontier. 'They are first mentioned by Cassius Dio in the context of the campaign of Roman emperor Caracalla of 213 AD'; Alamannia page: they 'had broken through the Roman limes in 213' and 'expanded from the Main River basin during the 3rd century'. The page gives no founding act; the confederation is dated by its first mention and its land is the researcher's reading of the Main basin.

region.text: the Agri Decumates, 'covering the Black Forest, Swabian Jura, and Franconian Jura areas between the Rhine, Main, and Danube rivers', with the Main basin

ledger.note: 260: the Alemanni take the Agri Decumates. 'the Alemanni captured the Agri Decumates in 260 AD'; the Agri Decumates page: 'Gallienus (259-260) evacuated it before the invading Alemanni'; Germanic Wars page: '259-260 Evacuation of the agrarian area Agri Decumates by the Roman Empire, Roman Empire retreats behind the Rhine'. The region is the gazetteer's Baden-Wurttemberg plus Franconia for 'Black Forest, Swabian Jura, and Franconian Jura'.

region.text: the Agri Decumates south of the Main: 'Emperor Probus definitely recaptured the area during his invasion of Germania'

ledger.note: 277: Probus retakes the Agri Decumates. 'Emperor Probus definitely recaptured the area during his invasion of Germania' (no year on the page); Germanic Wars page: '277-278 Emperor Probus's successful campaigns against Goths, Alamanni, Longiones, Franks and Burgundians'. 277 is the roman-empire dossier's year, bridged from the campaign dates. [Fix 2026-10-19: the Probus page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probus_(emperor)) dates his Alemannic campaign to 278 ('In 278, Probus campaigned successfully in Gaul against the Alemanni and Lugii'), after which he 'crossed the Rhine to campaign successfully in their homeland' and 'repaired the ancient fortifications erected by Hadrian in the vulnerable territory of Swabia'; so 277-278 is the bracket and 277 is kept only to match roman-empire /ledger/100 (gain from Alemanni, 277).]

region.text: the Agri Decumates, 'definitively abandoned' by the Roman military

ledger.note: about 300: the Agri Decumates are abandoned for good. 'the Roman military seems to have definitively abandoned the region' in 'the 290s or 300s'; 'By about 310 the Alemanni were becoming the dominant population'. The year 300 is bridged between those two statements; the roman-empire dossier uses about 300 as well. [Fix 2026-10-19: the Limes Germanicus page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limes_Germanicus) was opened for a year and gives none: it has the frontier 'from about 83 AD to 260 AD' and the Upper Raetian Limes lost in the 'late third century'; 300 stays a conf-1 bridge.]

region.text: 'what is today Alsace' (the page adds 'and a large part of the Swiss Plateau', not drawn: no gazetteer name)

ledger.note: 406: the Alemanni cross the Rhine and take Alsace. 'In the great mixed invasion of 406, the Alemanni appear to have crossed the Rhine river a final time, conquering and then settling what is today Alsace and a large part of the Swiss Plateau.' The year is the page's, hedged ('appear to have'); the region is the researcher's reading (Alsace named, the Swiss Plateau not drawn). The western-roman-empire dossier should carry the matching loss (its /ledger/50 gives the Rhine region to kingdom-of-alamannia only in 462, conf 1).

region.text: the Alemanni's land (Agri Decumates, Main basin and Alsace) passing to the Kingdom of Alamannia

ledger.note: 461/462: the Alemanni become the Kingdom of Alamannia. The pages date neither a founding of a kingdom nor a break: the cut is the start of the Cliopatria row (462); 'Gibuld (fl. 470) is the last known king of the Alemanni' and the Alemanni were 'defeated by Clovis I of the Franks at the Battle of Tolbiac' in 496 (Alamannia page).

wars.name: Alemannic invasion of Italy and the evacuation of the Agri Decumates
wars.outcome: Gallienus defeated the Alemanni at Mediolanum in 259 ('300,000 Alemanni die'), yet the Romans evacuated the Agri Decumates and retreated behind the Rhine in 259-260, and the Alemanni captured them in 260.
wars.note: Alemanni page: 'Emperor Gallienus defeats the Alemanni to rescue Rome' (259).

wars.name: Alemannic invasion of Gaul and northern Italy
wars.outcome: Claudius II defeated the Alemanni at Lake Benacus in 268; Aurelian was defeated by the Alemanni invading Italy at Placentia in 271 and the Alemannic army was destroyed in 271. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Alemanni page: 'launched a major invasion of Gaul and northern Italy in 268'; Germanic Wars page: '271 Destruction of Alemannic army'.

wars.name: Probus's campaigns against the Alamanni

zones.text: the Agri Decumates, recaptured by Probus

wars.outcome: Probus's 'successful campaigns against Goths, Alamanni, Longiones, Franks and Burgundians' (Germanic Wars page); the Agri Decumates page: Probus 'definitely recaptured the area'.
wars.note: The year of the recapture is not on the Agri Decumates page.

wars.name: Julian's campaigns against the Alemanni (Battle of Strasbourg)
wars.outcome: Roman double victory under Constantius II in 354-355; Siege of Autun 356; 'Roman invasion of Alemannic territory led by general Barbatio and Julian' in 357 and Julian 'expels the Alemanni from the Rhineland' at Strasbourg (357); several Alemannic kings 'in 359 made treaties with Julian the Apostate'. No lasting change of land is recorded on the pages.
wars.note: Alemanni page: 'Chnodomarius was the leader of the Alemannic army in the battle of Strasbourg in 357' (Alamannia page).

wars.name: Valentinian I's campaigns against the Alemanni
wars.outcome: The Alemanni crossed the frozen Rhine on 2 January 366 after the invasion of Gaul in 365 and the sack of Moguntiacum in 367; Valentinian invaded 'Alemannic territory' in 368 (Solicinium) and Macrian was 'deposed in an expedition ordered by Valentinian I in 370'. No land changed hands on the pages.
wars.note: Alemanni page: '368 Romans under Emperor Valentinian I defeat an Alemanni incursion'; '378 Western Emperor Gratianus is victorious over the Alemanni' (Argentovaria); Germanic Wars page: '378 Invasion of Alsace by Alemanni'.

wars.name: Alemannic invasion of Italy (Campi Cannini)
wars.outcome: 'Alemanni invade Italy and are defeated near Lake Maggiore by Majorian' (457).

certainty.note: No page draws the Alemannic frontier; the Agri Decumates follow the Roman limes line (Rheinbrohl to Pforring) only from the Roman side.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks before 462: its row Kingdom of Alamannia (eu-06, 462-731) starts after the Alemanni had held the Agri Decumates for two centuries. Four pages opened. Cut at 461 only because of Cliopatria's start: treat this dossier as the earlier life of the same state and link it as predecessor of kingdom-of-alamannia (or merge them; one colour for life). The pages give no capital and no ruler list, so capitals is empty and no rulers are listed (named kings: Chrocus, died 306 per the Alamannia page; Chnodomarius, 357; Westralp, 357; Macrian, deposed 370; Gibuld, fl. 470). Alsace is drawn from 406 (reviewer fix 2026-10-19; Alemanni page: 'In the great mixed invasion of 406, the Alemanni appear to have crossed the Rhine river a final time, conquering and then settling what is today Alsace and a large part of the Swiss Plateau'). The Swiss Plateau is not drawn (no gazetteer name; Switzerland would include the Alps) and the Alamannia page's undated 'left bank from the 4th century' is not drawn before 406; Cliopatria's 462 shape (bbox 3.7-10.2 E) and the western-roman-empire dossier's 462 loss of the Rhine region (conf 1) carry the rest. The matching 406 loss of Alsace is for the western-roman-empire dossier (eu-04-a). Wikidata id unknown. Gazetteer: 'Agri Decumates' is not a region name (Baden-Wurttemberg plus Franconia stand in); 'Raetia' and 'Pannonia' are not region names.
